name: site_audit
description: Keep the client list and the audit history for website audits, and build the report from a run's captured archives

tools.name: add_client
tools.description: Add a website to the audit roster. Pages are added afterwards, one at a time, with add_page

params.name: name
params.description: The client's display name, as it should read in the report

params.name: base_url
params.description: The site's home page. This sets the crawl boundary — URLs outside it are status-checked but never followed

params.name: slug
params.description: Short handle used in file paths and when asking for this client. Derived from the name when omitted, so set it when you want something shorter

params.name: cloudflare_project
params.description: Cloudflare Pages project the report publishes to. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only. Defaults to the slug followed by -audit

params.name: cloudflare_production_branch
params.description: Branch whose deployments publish to the live report. Any other branch becomes a preview. Left unset, the project's own production branch is used

params.name: crawl
params.description: Run the whole-site link check as part of an audit. It costs no API quota, only time

params.name: crawl_depth
params.description: How many clicks from a scored page the link check follows links

params.name: deep_dive
params.description: Include the manual review checklist in the report, for an audit a human will finish by hand

params.name: notes
params.description: Anything worth remembering about this client

tools.output_description: The slug the client was stored under, the record as written, and the file it was written to

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: List every website on the audit roster, with how many pages each has and when it was last audited
tools.output_description: A clients array of {slug, name, base_url, page_count, crawl, last_run, last_status} and a count

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: Look up one audit client in full, including the page list an audit will score

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

tools.output_description: The slug and the full client record: name, base_url, cloudflare_project, cloudflare_production_branch, crawl, crawl_depth, deep_dive, notes and pages[{label, url, slug}]

tools.name: update_client
tools.description: Change settings on an audit client. Only the fields you give are touched; the rest are left as they are. Use add_page and remove_page for the page list

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: name
params.description: New display name. The slug does not change with it

params.name: base_url
params.description: New home page, which moves the crawl boundary

params.name: cloudflare_project
params.description: Cloudflare Pages project the report publishes to

params.name: cloudflare_production_branch
params.description: Branch whose deployments publish to the live report

params.name: crawl
params.description: Whether an audit runs the whole-site link check

params.name: crawl_depth
params.description: How many clicks from a scored page the link check follows links

params.name: deep_dive
params.description: Whether the report includes the manual review checklist

params.name: notes
params.description: Replacement notes

params.name: clear
params.description: Fields to reset to their default instead of setting. An empty value cannot do this, because an empty param reads as one that was never given

items.name: field
items.description: Name of a field to reset

tools.output_description: The slug, which fields changed, which were cleared, and the updated record

tools.name: remove_client
tools.description: Take a website off the audit roster. Its past runs are kept unless you ask for them too

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: delete_runs
params.description: Also delete every recorded run for this client and the archives stored with them. This cannot be undone

tools.output_description: The slug removed, how many runs were deleted or kept, and the bytes reclaimed

tools.name: add_page
tools.description: Add a page to the list an audit scores for a client

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: label
params.description: How the page is named in the report

params.name: url
params.description: The page's full URL. It must be absolute — the client's base_url is not joined onto it

params.name: slug
params.description: Name for this page's archive files. Derived from the URL path when omitted, which is nearly always right

tools.output_description: The page as stored, the client's slug, and the new page count

tools.name: remove_page
tools.description: Take a page off the list an audit scores for a client

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: page
params.description: The page to remove, named by its label, its slug, or its URL

tools.output_description: The page that was removed and the client's remaining page count

tools.name: record_run
tools.description: Create or advance the record of an audit run. Only the fields you give are written, so a later call can report progress without resending what is already known. A run accumulates, so archives are added to and scores and sitemap are merged in rather than replacing what is there

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: date
params.description: The run's date as YYYY-MM-DD, which is what identifies it. Defaults to today

params.name: status
params.description: Where the run has got to. Reaching deployed, failed or cancelled stamps finished_at

params.name: crawl_job_id
params.description: Job id sitecrawl.start returned, so the sweep can ask how the crawl is getting on

params.name: archives
params.description: Archive filenames captured into the run's directory

items.name: filename
items.description: A filename sitting beside the run's record

params.name: scores
params.description: PageSpeed scores for this run, keyed however the caller finds useful

params.name: sitemap
params.description: What the crawl made of the sitemap: how many URLs it held, how many were reached, and whether the unreached ones were only sampled

params.name: progress
params.description: How far the run has got within the stage it is in — pages scored so far, or what the crawl has checked and discovered. Name the stage in a phase key so a reader knows what the numbers count. A snapshot, so each call replaces the last and the time it was taken is stamped on it; an empty object clears it

params.name: scan_failures
params.description: Pages this pass could not score, and why. A snapshot, so each call replaces the last and an empty array clears it — a page that scores on a later pass stops being listed

items.name: failure
items.description: The page and strategy that failed, with the reason

params.name: complete
params.description: Whether this run covered the site fully. False when a cap, a sample or a block means the findings are partial, which the report must say

params.name: deployed_url
params.description: Where the published report can be read

params.name: error
params.description: What went wrong, for a run that failed

params.name: notes
params.description: Anything worth recording about this particular run

tools.output_description: The client slug, the run date, whether the record was created or updated, which fields were written, and the record as it now stands

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List recorded audit runs, newest first, for one client or across all of them

params.name: client
params.description: Limit to one client, by slug, display name or hostname. Omit for every client

params.name: limit
params.description: How many runs to return. 0 returns all of them

tools.output_description: A runs array of {client, date, status, complete, deployed_url, started_at, finished_at, archive_count} newest first, and a count

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Read one audit run in full, including what it captured and where it published

params.name: client
params.description: The client's slug, display name, or the hostname of its site

params.name: date
params.description: The run's date as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to the most recent run

tools.output_description: The client slug, the run date, the full run record, the archives stored with it, the directory they live in, and its size in bytes

tools.name: prune_runs
tools.description: Delete old audit runs and the archives stored with them, to stop the data directory growing without bound. Runs that have not finished are never touched

params.name: client
params.description: Prune one client only, by slug, display name or hostname. Omit to prune every client

params.name: keep
params.description: How many of the most recent runs to keep per client regardless of age

params.name: older_than_days
params.description: Only delete runs older than this many days. 0 ignores age and keeps only the most recent ones

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Report what would be deleted without deleting anything

tools.output_description: How many runs were deleted, kept, and left alone for being unfinished, the bytes reclaimed, the runs involved per client, and whether this was a dry run

tools.name: build_report
tools.description: Turn a run's captured archives into the report site: scores, issues, screenshots and the link worklist, ready for Jekyll to render. Reads only what is already on disk, so it is free to re-run

params.name: raw_dir
params.description: Directory holding the captured archives: one gzipped PageSpeed report per page and form factor, and crawl.json.gz if the site was crawled

params.name: site_dir
params.description: Where to build the report. Created from the seed templates the first time. Everything derived here is wiped and rebuilt on every call, so point it at nothing else

params.name: pages
params.description: The pages to report on, in the order they should read. Worked out from the archives when omitted, which loses only the labels

properties.name: label
properties.description: How the page is named in the report

properties.name: slug
properties.description: Name of this page's archive files. Derived from the URL path when omitted

params.name: report
params.description: What the report calls itself. Falls back to a manifest.json sitting with the archives, then to defaults

properties.name: title
properties.description: Name shown in the report's header, usually the site's owner

properties.name: site_url
properties.description: The site the report is about

properties.name: date
properties.description: The date the report is for, as YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today

properties.name: notes
properties.description: Any note to carry into the report

params.name: categories
params.description: Render only these Lighthouse categories. Everything present in the archive, when omitted. A filter on rendering only — the archive is untouched

params.name: deep_dive
params.description: Include the manual-review layer: the full scope callout and a notes stub per page, for an audit a human will finish by hand

params.name: no_lighthouse
params.description: Render without any scores, producing a link audit from the crawl alone. A rendering filter only, so dropping it brings the scores back

params.name: no_links
params.description: Render without the link findings even though the site was crawled. A rendering filter only

params.name: reseed
params.description: Copy the current seed templates over an existing report before building, to pull template fixes into a run already on disk. Hand-written findings are never touched; template edits made inside the run are overwritten

params.name: seed_dir
params.description: Build from a different set of templates than the ones shipped with this module

tools.output_description: Where the report was built, whether it was scaffolded or reseeded, what the report calls itself, the categories rendered, counts of pages, issues and screenshots, a summary of the link findings including whether coverage was partial, the files written, and any warnings — a report that is a link audit rather than a full one says so here
